text:
Maria (Eng Ops): Quick follow-up from today's all-hands demo: people asked if the new 2-week release pilot is a change to our oncall expectations and SLA commitments. Can leadership clarify?

Srini (VP Eng): Short: pilot only. We want faster iteration for infra-heavy teams (runtime/infra) without sacrificing reliability. No customer SLA changes. Internally, teams must meet the same SLOs.

Josh (PM): Pilot rules we're using: 1) smaller PRs, 2) mandatory canary rollout + auto-rollback, 3) perf baseline attached to PR, 4) QA checklist included. Teams not in pilot keep the 4-week cadence.

Devon (SRE): For teams in the pilot, how does oncall shift? Will we get extra rotations for deploy windows?

Srini (VP Eng): Deploy-window rotations: the team on a 2-week cadence assigns a deploy owner for the rollout window (same as current deploy-oncall model), and SRE remains escalation. We will not increase overall oncall headcount immediately; teams should stagger deploys. Eng Ops will publish a schedule.

Anya (Head QA): Quality bar specifics from the pilot: no new P0/P1 test failures, smoke e2e green within 10m post-deploy, and p95 for critical paths must be within 15% of baseline (we used 10% in the internal trial but leaving some wiggle room). Any persistent flaky tests must be quarantined and linked in PR.

Maria (Eng Ops): Where are the templates/runbooks?

Oncall Bot: Links pinned: https://intranet.redwood.example/pilot-guides/2-week-release and https://intranet.redwood.example/runbooks/deploy-fallback (pinned in #eng-oncall).

Josh (PM): Example canary plan to include in PR: 5% for 15m, 25% for 45m, 75% for 3h, 100% in 12h. Auto-rollback triggers: error rate delta >0.4% OR p95 > 120% of baseline for 10m. These are defaults; teams must justify changes in PR description.

Devon (SRE): Strong ask: default fallback should be last-known-good. Also please add an automated post-deploy smoke that posts its status back to the PR thread. Manual checks are error-prone.

Srini (VP Eng): Agreed: fallback to last-known-good is default. We'll require a smoke job as part of the pipeline for pilot teams; it must post results and the perf snapshot.

Anya (Head QA): We'll produce a short checklist doc for PRs: unit tests, integration smoke, perf delta screenshot, flaky-test table, ops signoff if infra changes.

Maria (Eng Ops): And customer-facing SLAs? Any change to public promises?

Srini (VP Eng): No changes. Public SLAs remain intact. Internally, product and support will be notified of release schedule; any regressions affecting customers trigger the usual incident playbooks.

Josh (PM): Pilot cohort: runtime, eng-platform, and data-pipelines. We'll run three release cycles and then review telemetry: rollback rate, incident count, time-to-release, and dev throughput.

Devon (SRE): Can we define rollback telemetry threshold for pausing the pilot?

Srini (VP Eng): If rollback rate > 15% or customer-impacting incidents increase > 50% over baseline across two consecutive cycles, we'll pause and retro. Data team will pull metrics weekly.

Maria (Eng Ops): I'll collate these notes into a short FAQ and link the templates. If folks have objections or edge cases (eg: large infra migrations), please ping me or @Srini. Closing this thread but will post the FAQ shortly. :white_check_mark:
